description: Compact feed of currently active NasDecode Market Watch catalysts.

activeEvents.companyMarket: US inflation / GDP / Fed / Treasuries / SOX / Nasdaq
activeEvents.headline: October core PCE rises to 3.3% year over year; Q3 GDP revised up to 4.3% annualized
activeEvents.whyItMatters: Core PCE exceeded the 3.2% consensus while headline PCE reached 3.8% as expected. GDP was revised from 3.4% to 4.3%, above the 3.6% forecast. Together these reinforce the case for December Fed tightening, although stronger activity supports demand. Official PCE release: https://bea.gov/sites/default/files/2026-11/pi1026.pdf

activeEvents.headline: S&P places Nvidia AA credit rating on CreditWatch Negative over governance risks
activeEvents.whyItMatters: The rating agency may cut the rating one notch within 90 days; governance and succession concerns could increase financing costs for Nvidia and AI projects relying on its credit support. No downgrade has occurred. Moody's maintained its rating and stable outlook. Independent coverage: https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/25/sp-considers-nvidia-credit-downgrade-over-governance-and-key-man-risks/

activeEvents.companyMarket: US trade policy / China / EU / Asian semiconductor supply chains / Nasdaq
activeEvents.headline: US formally proposes Section 301 tariffs on 14 trading partners following overcapacity investigation
activeEvents.whyItMatters: Formal proposals replace earlier speculation. Proposed maximum rates include Vietnam 35%, India 25%, China 20%, and Taiwan, South Korea, Japan and EU 15%, subject to trade arrangements and product-specific treatment. Hearings begin January 25, 2027; duties are not yet effective and do not stack on certain July Section 301 tariffs. Technology supply-chain costs and inflation risks depend on final scope and exemptions. Corroboration: https://www.conference-board.org/publications/tariff-tracker

activeEvents.companyMarket: Nvidia (NVDA) / China AI accelerators / SOX / Nasdaq
activeEvents.headline: Reuters reports Nvidia China customers cancel or delay orders following leadership crisis and renewed US scrutiny
activeEvents.whyItMatters: Reuters reports some Chinese buyers are cancelling or delaying orders for Nvidia's export-compliant AI products following Jensen Huang's resignation and intensified US scrutiny. China/Hong Kong customer revenue reportedly rose to $11.05 billion in the quarter ended October 25, 2026 from $2.97 billion a year earlier, making potential demand erosion financially material. The scope of cancellations is not quantified and should not be equated with a company-wide revenue guidance cut.

activeEvents.companyMarket: CrowdStrike (CRWD) / Zscaler (ZS) / cloud and AI cybersecurity / Nasdaq
activeEvents.headline: CrowdStrike and Zscaler sign definitive $43.9 billion all-stock cybersecurity acquisition agreement
activeEvents.whyItMatters: The signed deal combines CrowdStrike endpoint security with Zscaler's cloud network and zero-trust platform, expanding cybersecurity consolidation and competition in AI-agent security. Zscaler holders are offered 1.135 CRWD shares per ZS share; closing remains conditional on shareholder and regulatory approvals. Management projects over $10 billion combined annual recurring revenue and eventual cross-sell synergies, which are forecasts rather than realized results.

activeEvents.companyMarket: Taiwan equity market / TSM / semiconductor supply chain / SOX / Nasdaq
activeEvents.headline: Taiwan deploys stabilization fund, tightens short selling and eases margin-call requirements amid AI-chip selloff
activeEvents.scope: Taiwan equities and global semiconductor sentiment
activeEvents.whyItMatters: Taiwan authorities have deployed their approximately $15 billion equity stabilization fund and increased short-sale margin requirements from 130% to 150% during a severe AI and semiconductor selloff. Taiwan hosts TSMC and key AI hardware suppliers, making the intervention a material cross-market liquidity and sentiment development, distinct from previously archived export-control news. South Korea is preparing possible stabilization measures, but those are not treated as already deployed. Reuters reported November 23 that Taiwan will also reduce the minimum margin-maintenance ratio from 130% to 120% starting Tuesday, November 24, explicitly lowering the risk of forced liquidations. This is an additional implemented policy announcement, distinct from the previously recorded short-sale margin increase.

activeEvents.headline: Nvidia board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO; semiconductor stocks surge
activeEvents.whyItMatters: The reported unanimous board decision reverses the leadership departure and reduces immediate management uncertainty. Investigations and export-control risks remain unresolved.
